facts.text: Sky Crane Descent Stage was deployed at Gale Crater during Curiosity (MSL) in 2012.

The sky crane hover stage lowered Curiosity on 7.6-metre nylon tethers, then flew away to crash-land 650 metres from the rover. This was the first use of the sky crane landing system. HiRISE images from orbit show the dark blast marks where its retrorockets hit the surface. The wreckage remains where it fell.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Demonstrated the first-ever sky crane landing, proving that heavy payloads can be precision-delivered to the Martian surface.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Gale Crater.
The wreckage and blast marks are visible from orbit via HiRISE; the sky crane design was reused for Perseverance in 2021.
